title: registry-item.json — module descriptor
description: shadcn-shaped descriptor authored in the CLI/registry repo. The applier reads it off disk to resolve dependencies, apply files + npm deps + patches, and copy the module's skill folder(s) into .claude/skills/ (build spec §3.3).

$schema.description: Optional pointer to this schema for editor validation.

name.description: Module name (lowercase, digits, hyphens). Unique within the registry.

type.description: `saasaloy:capability` scaffolds an app/package and establishes extension points; `saasaloy:feature` extends capabilities by dropping files into their conventions.

requires.description: Tool versions this descriptor needs. A descriptor sets `additionalProperties: false`, so an old CLI meeting a new field already fails — as a raw schema dump, and not at all when an existing field merely changed meaning. Declaring a range turns both into one fatal, actionable message, checked before any write is planned. Optional: a descriptor without it works on every CLI version.

saasaloy.description: Semver range the running `saasaloy` CLI has to satisfy (e.g. `>=0.3`, `>=0.3 <2`, `^1.2.0`, `1.x`). Any range shape is accepted, upper bounds included, so there is no separate maximum field. A CLI outside the range refuses the whole run and names this module, even when it is a transitive `dependsOn`.

dependsOn.description: Modules this one requires. Resolved recursively and topologically sorted behind a confirmation prompt.

conflictsWith.description: Modules this one refuses to sit beside — two implementations of the same capability, say. `add` refuses with a message naming both modules when a conflicting module is already installed. Either side may declare it: the field is recorded into saasaloy-lock.json, so the refusal fires in either install order. Never auto-resolved; `add` uninstalls nothing.

requiresOneOf.description: Modules exactly one of which has to be present — a capability naming its mutually exclusive drivers (e.g. `database` naming `database-d1` and `database-postgres`). `add` counts a module as present when it is already installed or arrives in the same resolved graph, refuses when none is, and offers the list as a prompt on an interactive terminal. Use `dependsOn` for a single hard prerequisite; this field exists for a choice, so it takes at least two names (#98, ADR 0026).

dependencies.description: npm packages merged into the consumer's `dependencies`. Each must be exact-pinned `name@version` (e.g. zod@4.0.5) — bare names and ranges are rejected; `pnpm deps:update` fills/refreshes the versions.

devDependencies.description: npm packages merged into the consumer's `devDependencies` (e.g. @types/*, build tooling). Same exact-pinned `name@version` form as `dependencies`. A name declared in both buckets lands in `dependencies` only.

files.description: Files to copy into the project. `path` is relative to the module folder; `target` resolves through the project's alias map.

path.description: Source path relative to the module folder (e.g. files/api/routes/waitlist.ts). No '.' or '..' path segment: the applier refuses one at runtime and this fails the descriptor at authoring time (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .gitignore is fine.

target.description: Alias-prefixed destination (e.g. @api/routes/waitlist.ts). No '.' or '..' path segment: the applier refuses one at runtime and this fails the descriptor at authoring time (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .gitignore is fine.

onlyWith.description: Install this file only when the named module is in the resolved install set — this run's dependsOn graph plus what saasaloy.json already records (#99). Two entries may share one `target` when their conditions are disjoint: that is how a module ships a per-driver variant of a dialect-bound file. A target whose entries are all conditional and none matches is a plan-time refusal, not a silently missing file.

envVars.description: Environment variables the module needs: NAME → human description (or default/placeholder).

devVars.description: Local-development values for a subset of `envVars`: NAME → the value `saasaloy add` pre-fills into the generated `apps/api/.dev.vars.example`. Only for a value that is the same on every machine and is not a secret (a loopback URL, a fixed port). Every key here must also appear in `envVars`; a key absent here is written with an empty value for the owner to fill in.

removeWarnings.description: Warnings saved with an installed module and shown before removal. Use this for deployed resources that file and patch removal cannot delete safely.

patches.description: Structural config patches applied at `add` time by the patch engine (issue #7). A flat array where each op names its own target `file` and codemod `kind` (wrangler.jsonc bindings, package.json dependency merges, package.json script entries, Better Auth plugin-array insertions, router chain `.route()` links); kind-specific payload fields are defined by the engine. An empty array means no patches (ADR 0019).

file.description: Project-relative POSIX path of the file to patch (e.g. apps/api/wrangler.jsonc). No leading slash or @alias, and no '.' or '..' path segment (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .eslintrc.json is fine.

kind.description: Which codemod applies this patch. `const-array`, `plugin-array`, and `chained-route` have removal inverses.

constName.description: Name of the module-scope const array to extend.

key.description: Entry property whose JSON value identifies the entry for add and remove.

entry.description: JSON object literal appended to the named array.

name.description: Script key to upsert into the target's `scripts` map (e.g. db:generate).

value.description: Command the script runs (e.g. drizzle-kit generate). An entry already present under this key is never overwritten.

exportName.description: Exported binding whose call chain to extend — `default`, or the name in `export const <name> = …`. A bare `export default app` is followed to its declaration.

path.description: Route path — `.route()`'s first argument (e.g. /waitlist). Also the match key: a chain already routing this path is left alone, and `remove` finds the link by it.

call.description: Identifier passed as `.route()`'s second argument (e.g. waitlist) — the sub-router the import supplies.

import.description: Named import to add for `call`, dropped again on `remove` (with its statement, when it was the only specifier).

scaffolds.description: New workspaces a capability module creates (apps/packages). Each entry births one workspace: copies its files to workspace-root-relative targets and registers the aliases it declares into saasaloy.json (ADR 0013).

workspace.description: New workspace directory, project-relative POSIX (e.g. apps/api). No leading slash or @alias.

aliases.description: Alias → path-prefix map this scaffold registers into saasaloy.json (e.g. { "@api": "apps/api/src" }).

additionalProperties.description: Project-relative path prefix (POSIX separators, no leading slash).

files.description: Files copied into the workspace. `path` is relative to the module folder; `target` is relative to the workspace root (no @alias — the alias root doesn't exist yet).

path.description: Source path relative to the module folder (e.g. files/src/index.ts). No '.' or '..' path segment: the applier refuses one at runtime and this fails the descriptor at authoring time (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .dev.vars.example is fine.

target.description: Destination relative to the workspace root (e.g. src/index.ts). No leading slash or @alias, and no '.' or '..' path segment (#98). A dot-leading file name such as .dev.vars.example is fine.

onlyWith.description: Install this file only when the named module is in the resolved install set — this run's dependsOn graph plus what saasaloy.json already records (#99). Same rule as a top-level files[] entry: two entries may share one `target` when their conditions are disjoint, and a target no candidate matches is a plan-time refusal. auth's per-driver db-provider.ts lives here rather than in files[], which is why both shapes carry the keyword.

agent.description: AI context contributed by this module. A module ships skill folder(s) that `add` copies into .claude/skills/ (recorded in the manifest for a clean `remove`); it never edits the committed AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.

skills.description: Skill folder(s) relative to the module folder, copied into .claude/skills/.
